name: polar-bear-skills
title: Claude Skills — themed skill packs for Claude Code and Claude.ai
description: A marketplace of themed Claude Skill (Agent Skill) packs. Each pack bundles SKILL.md skills and shared reference files around one job to be done.

install.claudeAi: Settings → Customize → Skills → Upload skill, using the zips in each pack's install/ folder

license: Free to use inside your company, not for resale.

packs.name: proposals-pack
packs.title: The Proposals Pack
packs.description: 12 Claude Skills for writing a proposal deck the client can decide from, section by section, from an RFP or from your team's own notes, ending in a .pptx: the firm context file, the brief that separates facts from assumptions, the storyline as action titles, the context, market, problem, vision, approach, team and investment sections, the deck build on your template, and the review from the client's chair.

resources.description: Filled once by a founder or a lead with firm-context-writer: what the firm does and refuses, its ideal client, the credentials library with real outcomes only, the team roster, the cost basis behind its prices, who approves what, and the deck conventions. Every other skill reads it before writing a word.

The blank proposal-brief-builder fills from an RFP or the team's notes, one per opportunity. A team can also fill it by hand and hand it straight to storyline-designer. Every section skill draws from it; if a fact is not in the brief, it does not go on a slide.

skills.name: firm-context-writer
skills.summary: Interviews you and writes firm-context.md, the ground-truth file every other skill reads: what the firm does and refuses, the ideal client, the credentials library with real outcomes only, the team roster, the cost basis behind prices, who approves what, and the deck conventions.

skills.name: proposal-brief-builder
skills.summary: Turns whatever arrived, an RFP, an email, call notes or a founder's paragraph, into the brief every section skill reads: the ask in one sentence, who decides and how, the requirements matrix, known facts with sources, the assumptions register, and the firm's angle. Flags a thin brief and drafts the questions to fill it.
triggers: here's what we know, build the brief
extract the requirements from this RFP
we need to write something for Acme by Friday

skills.name: storyline-designer
skills.summary: Writes the ghost deck before any content exists: the executive summary, which sections this client needs, an action title for every slide, the evidence each title needs, and the slide budget.

skills.summary: Writes the “your situation and objectives” section in the client's own words, with every fact sourced to the brief and every inference marked as an assumption on the slide.

triggers: add market context to the proposal

skills.name: problem-section-writer
skills.summary: Writes the problem as a diagnosis rather than a restatement of the RFP: symptoms, hypotheses about causes labeled tested or untested, what it costs the client, and what the proposal will and will not solve.

skills.name: vision-section-writer
skills.summary: Writes the answer and the target picture as a position rather than a service list: what will be different, the principles the firm will hold, the two or three big moves, and why this answer fits this client.

skills.name: approach-section-writer
skills.summary: Writes phases, deliverables, timeline, governance, the client's role, and risks, keeping dates and named people as drafts until the person who approves the promise says yes.

skills.name: team-section-writer
skills.summary: Writes the team and credentials section: who is on this engagement and why each fits, plus two or three cases that mirror the client's situation, drawn from the credentials library with real outcomes only, kept short and placed after the work.

skills.name: investment-section-writer
skills.summary: Writes one to three honest options that differ in scope and outcome, the price of each from the firm's approved numbers, the assumptions behind the price, terms, and next steps with dates. No decoys, no invented market rates.

skills.name: deck-builder
skills.summary: Assembles the section files into proposal-[client].pptx on the firm's template through code execution: one slide per action title, executive summary and dividers, a source line on every data slide, assumptions kept visible, speaker notes, and the requirements cross-reference for RFPs.

skills.name: deck-reviewer
skills.summary: Reads the built deck from the client's chair and against the brief — the storyline from the titles alone, unsourced claims, unanswered requirements, the firm talking about itself too early, numbers that do not add up — and returns an edit list rather than a rewrite.
